one_fourth_carbs.definition: 1/4 of the meal is starchy foods. Starchy foods include all fresh, frozen, and canned starchy vegetables such as breadfruit, burdock root, cassava, corn, jicama, lotus root, lima beans, immature or raw peas, plantains, white potatoes, salsify, tapioca, taro, water chestnuts, yam, yucca, butternut, kabocha, and pumpkin. They also include legumes and pulses such as lentils, beans, and peas; all grain products and grains used as ingredients such as amaranth, barley, buckwheat, bulgur, millet, oats, popcorn, quinoa, dark rye, triticale, cornmeal, breads, tortilla, flatbread, chapati, cereals, crackers, corn grits, cream of rice, cream of wheat, masa, pasta, noodles, popcorn, and rice. Also included are 1 cup milk, yogurt, or fortified soymilk with high sugar content; fruits with high sugar content; sweets and desserts such as brownies, cake, cupcakes, cookies, gelatin, pie, pudding, sweeteners, candy, coffee creamer, fruit snacks, fruit spreads, honey, jam, jelly, sugar, syrup, doughnuts, muffins, pastries, sweet breads, frozen bars, frozen desserts, frozen yogurt, and ice cream; and sweetened beverages.

half_fruits_vegetables.definition: At least 1/2 cup-equivalent of fruit and 1 cup-equivalent of non-starchy vegetables in the meal. One cup-equivalent of vegetables and fruits means 1 cup raw or cooked vegetable or fruit, 1 cup vegetable or fruit juice, 2 cups leafy salad greens, or 1/2 cup dried fruit or vegetable. Include all fresh, frozen, and canned non-starchy vegetables, cooked or raw, and 100% vegetable juices. Examples include dark-green vegetables such as amaranth leaves, basil, beet greens, bitter melon leaves, bok choy, broccoli, chamnamul, chrysanthemum leaves, chard, cilantro, collards, cress, dandelion greens, kale, lambsquarters, mustard greens, poke greens, romaine lettuce, spinach, nettles, taro leaves, turnip greens, and watercress; non-starchy red and orange vegetables such as calabaza, carrots, red chili peppers, red or orange bell peppers, pimento, tomatoes, and 100% tomato juice; legumes such as black beans, garbanzo beans, kidney beans, soybeans, and tofu; and other vegetables such as artichoke, asparagus, avocado, bamboo shoots, bean sprouts, beets, bitter melon, broccoflower, Brussels sprouts, cabbage, cactus pads, cauliflower, celeriac, celery, chayote, chives, cucumber, eggplant, fennel bulb, garlic, ginger root, green beans, iceberg lettuce, kohlrabi, leeks, luffa, mushrooms, okra, onions, peppers that are not red or orange, radicchio, sprouted beans, radish, rutabaga, seaweed, snow peas, summer squash, tomatillos, turnips, and winter melons. Include all fresh, frozen, canned, and dried fruits and 100% fruit juices. Examples include apples, apricots, Asian pears, bananas, berries, citrus fruits, cherries, dates, figs, grapes, guava, jackfruit, lychee, mangoes, melons, nectarines, papaya, passion fruit, peaches, pears, persimmons, pineapple, plums, pomegranates, prunes, raisins, rhubarb, sapote, soursop, starfruit, and tamarind.

lean_protein.definition: Choose low-fat protein sources with 3 grams of fat or less per ounce. Lean protein sources include beef such as ground beef that is 90% or higher lean and select or choice grades trimmed of fat; poultry without skin such as chicken, Cornish hen, domestic duck or goose well-drained of fat, turkey, lean ground turkey, or lean ground chicken; lean pork such as Canadian bacon, ham, rib or loin chop or roast, and tenderloin; lamb chop, lamb leg, lamb roast, veal cutlet without breading, veal loin chop, veal roast; game such as buffalo, ostrich, rabbit, and venison; sausage, hot dog, and processed sandwich meats with 3 grams of fat or less per ounce such as chipped beef, thin-sliced deli meats, turkey ham, and turkey pastrami; organ meats such as heart, kidney, and liver; fresh or canned fish such as black sea bass, catfish, cod, flounder, haddock, halibut, orange roughy, tilapia, trout, salmon, sardines, tuna, smoked herring, or smoked salmon, while avoiding any fried fish; shellfish such as clams, crabs, imitation shellfish, lobster, scallops, shrimp, and oysters; low-fat or fat-free cheeses and curd-style cheeses; egg whites and plain egg substitutes; chicken and turkey breast without skin, or ground turkey breast, while avoiding any fried chicken; seafoods such as anchovy, catfish, clams, cod, crab, crawfish, flounder, haddock, hake, herring, lobster, mackerel, mullet, oyster, perch, pollock, salmon, sardine, scallop, shrimp, sole, squid, tilapia, freshwater trout, light tuna, and whiting; all cooked or canned, drained and rinsed beans, peas, and lentils without added fats or fatty meats, including black beans, garbanzo beans, kidney beans, lima beans, navy beans, pinto beans, white beans, lentils of any color, edamame, black-eyed peas, and split peas, but not including green beans or green peas; plant-based protein like meatless burger or deli slices, tofu; low-fat 1% or fat-free skim milk, yogurt, cottage cheese, fat-free cheeses, or fat-free cream cheeses; and egg whites or egg substitutes. Not low-fat protein sources include 85% or lower lean ground beef, corned beef, meatloaf, prime cuts of beef, short ribs, tongue; poultry with skin such as chicken, dove, pheasant, turkey, wild duck, goose, and turkey bacon; pork cutlet, ground pork, pork shoulder roast, pork bacon, sausage, spareribs; ground lamb and lamb rib roast; hot dogs made from beef, pork, turkey, or chicken; processed sandwich meats or sausage with more than 3 grams of fat per ounce such as bologna, hard salami, pastrami, bratwurst, chorizo, Italian sausage, knockwurst, Polish sausage, smoked sausage, and summer sausage; regular cheese or reduced-fat cheeses with more than 3 grams of fat per ounce such as American, blue-veined, brie, cheddar, feta, hard goat cheese, Monterey jack, mozzarella, Parmesan, pasteurized processed cheese spread, queso, Swiss, and regular or part skim ricotta; whole egg; falafel, hummus, tempeh, nuts, and nut spreads.
